groups.sentence: Instructors include a statement or policy on generative AI use in their course syllabus.
Programs, units and administrators set and communicate AI expectations and syllabus requirements for faculty and students.
Instructors clearly communicate to students whether and how AI may be used, and what is allowed and not allowed.
Instructors are specific in their AI policy, naming permitted and prohibited uses, tools, examples, rationale, and citation or disclosure rules.
Clear AI statements help students understand expectations, and missing guidance causes confusion.
Instructors communicate AI policies early, at course start, and often, both in writing and orally.
Instructors may choose their own approach to AI, add optional policy statements, and repeat policies elsewhere.
Instructors do not leave AI expectations ambiguous or assume students already know the rules.
Instructors state AI expectations in assignment instructions, marking where AI use is permitted or required, not only in the syllabus.
Instructors remind students of the AI policy repeatedly, for each assignment and throughout the semester.
Unclear or absent AI statements make it hard to address academic misconduct.
